Fit the calibration model

Source: R/calibrate.R
fit_calibration.Rd

Fits a calibration model to all the reviewed clips. The species and site levels of validations are stored with the model, so that score_detections() can score new detections.

Usage

fit_calibration(
  validations,
  formula,
  engine = c("lme4", "brms"),
  prior = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

validations

Table returned by read_validations().

formula

Model formula, usually the best one of compare_calibration_models().

engine

"lme4" or "brms".

prior

engine = "brms": the prior (a brmsprior object), e.g. from calibration_prior(). Required.

...

engine = "brms": further arguments for brms::brm() (e.g. chains, iter, cores, backend, seed).

Value

A glm, glmerMod or brmsfit model, with the attribute sheepdog_levels (the species and site levels), used by score_detections() and plot_calibration().

Details

With engine = "lme4" (default), the model is fitted by maximum likelihood ('lme4' for random effects, glm() otherwise). A model with random effects whose fit is singular (a variance estimated at zero or a correlation at +-1) raises a warning: the fixed effects and the predictions can still be used, but the variance components on the boundary should not be interpreted, and a simpler model may predict as well. Check them with lme4::VarCorr(). The other messages of lme4::glmer() are passed on, prefixed by lme4:, and every message of the fit is kept in the attribute sheepdog_messages of the model (convergence warnings of 'lme4' are warnings and are passed on as such).

With engine = "brms", the model is fitted in a Bayesian framework with 'brms' (Bernoulli family, logit link). The prior must be given explicitly; calibration_prior() builds an example centred on an already calibrated score. After the fit, calibration_diagnostics() runs and a warning is raised when R-hat, the effective sample sizes or the divergent transitions fail the usual limits. Check the prior with prior_predictive_calibration(), the fit with brms::pp_check() and the sensitivity to the prior with calibration_sensitivity().
